name: Company Law Directive
impact_assessment: None (codification); amendment IAs SWD(2018) 141 and SWD(2023) 178
evidence_rating: ex-ante only: codification with no promises of its own; amendment forecasts not yet evaluated; only descriptive mobility counts
summary: The 2017 Company Law Directive merely consolidated older rules, so it set no targets of its own. Later amendments promised EUR 42-84 million in savings from online company registration and about EUR 437 million a year from easier cross-border use of company data, but none has been evaluated. Independent counts show cross-border company moves remain concentrated in a few countries.

indicators.objective: Directive 2017/1132 is a codification (proposal COM(2015) 616) with no impact assessment or indicators. Substantive promises come from later amendments: digitalisation (2019/1151), cross-border mobility (2019/2121) and 'digitalisation 2.0' (2025/25)

indicators.indicator: Savings from online registration for new companies
indicators.evidence: Online formation applies since 2021-2023 (with extensions); no ex-post measurement of savings found.

indicators.target_or_baseline: Baseline 2000-2019: 4,305 cross-border mergers, 553 conversions, 19 divisions (concentrated in DE, NL, LU)
indicators.evidence: Independent counts exist up to 2023 (Biermeyer & Meyer series); no evaluation of the 2019 mobility rules yet.

indicators.target_or_baseline: about EUR 437m a year (forecast); one-off costs ~EUR 311m

literature.citation: European Commission (2018), Impact Assessment on the EU Company Law package (digital tools; cross-border conversions, mergers and divisions), executive summary, SWD(2018) 142 (full IA SWD(2018) 141)
literature.title: Impact Assessment on the EU Company Law package (digital tools; cross-border conversions, mergers and divisions), executive summary
literature.headline: Online registration expected to save new companies EUR 42-84m; harmonised cross-border conversion and division rules expected to benefit especially SMEs
literature.summary_plain: For the 2019 amendments the Commission forecast EUR 42-84 million in savings from registering companies online and easier cross-border moves for small firms.

literature.citation: European Commission (2023), Impact Assessment on further expanding and upgrading digital tools in company law, executive summary, SWD(2023) 179 (full IA SWD(2023) 178)
literature.title: Impact Assessment on further expanding and upgrading digital tools in company law, executive summary
literature.headline: Recurrent savings of about EUR 437m a year for companies operating cross-border; one-off costs of about EUR 311m for companies newly filing data; EUR 5.4m one-off for registers
literature.summary_plain: For the 2025 amendment the Commission forecast about EUR 437 million a year in savings for firms doing business across borders.

literature.citation: Biermeyer & Meyer (2019), Cross-border Corporate Mobility in the EU: Empirical Findings 2019 (Vol. 1), Maastricht University / SSRN 3403791
literature.title: Cross-border Corporate Mobility in the EU: Empirical Findings 2019 (Vol. 1)
literature.method: descriptive (case counts from registers and official journals)
literature.headline: 2000-2019: 4,305 cross-border mergers, 553 conversions, 158 SE seat transfers, 19 divisions; heavily concentrated in Germany, the Netherlands and Luxembourg, suggesting incomplete integration
literature.summary_plain: Researchers counted about 8,400 cross-border company moves between 2000 and 2019, concentrated in a few countries, a baseline for judging the 2019 mobility rules.

literature.title: The use of corporate mobility instruments and Brexit: An empirical analysis
literature.method: descriptive analysis of a hand-collected dataset of cross-border mergers and SE seat transfers out of the UK, 1 January 2017 to 30 November 2019
literature.outcomes: use of cross-border merger (Directive 2017/1132 Title II Ch. II) and SE seat-transfer instruments to relocate from the UK
literature.headline: Between January 2017 and November 2019, UK companies used cross-border mergers and SE seat transfers to move to other EU Member States, mainly in the financial sector but also in other sectors.
literature.summary_plain: Before Brexit, some UK companies used the EU's company-law tools for cross-border mergers to move into the EU. Most were financial firms, showing these legal routes were actually used when firms needed them.
literature.quality: Descriptive counts of instrument use, no counterfactual; concerns the cross-border merger rules codified in Directive 2017/1132. Abstract gives no counts. Same authors as the listed 2019 report but a separate article.
literature.citation: Thomas Biermeyer; Marcus Meyer (2020), The use of corporate mobility instruments and Brexit: An empirical analysis, European Company Law 17(1): 15-20
